title: Rethinking Courtship Dynamics and Male Leadership
author: Michael Foster
summary: Foster critiques both the 'you are the prize' and 'man must pursue' frameworks in courtship, proposing the dance metaphor as superior. He argues both slogans can devolve into unhealthy dynamics—ego-driven power games or desperate chasing. Foster advocates for balanced biblical marriage where man leads with steadiness, woman responds with enthusiasm, both with mutual respect. The piece emphasizes that true leadership and followership require order without rigidity; when the rhythm fails, forcing the relationship becomes destructive. Dance imagery captures both structure and responsiveness needed in healthy courtship.
points: Dance metaphor: man leads, woman responds; both active, neither passive or manipulative
You are the prize frame can feed ego and manipulation; avoid empty swagger
Pursuit frame can slide into chasing and desperation; pedestalizing ruins relationship balance
Woman is fellow image-bearer, not angelic being; appreciation must not become pedestalizing
Courtship is learning to dance and picking suited partner; testing rhythm matters early
quotes: Mutual respect, shared purpose, and clear standards matter more than slogans. A quality man is a prize. He just is not the prize. There is a massive difference.
If you follow my stuff, you know I like dance as a metaphor for marriage. The man leads, but the woman is never passive.
When it's working, it isn't rigid or awkward. It's coordinated. You can feel the rhythm.

Two people can respect each other and still not make a good pair. Once it's clear the rhythm isn't there, forcing it doesn't make you virtuous. It just sets you up for a long stretch of frustration and imbalance.
The goal isn't to make something work at all costs. The goal is a partnership where leadership and response actually fit together.” Archived from This is Foster on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
